questions.q: What do the four letters of the STAR method stand for?
options: Story, Topic, Analysis, Review
Situation, Task, Action, Result
Setup, Test, Act, Repeat
Summary, Technique, Approach, Resolution
questions.explain: STAR stands for Situation, Task, Action, Result — a structure for giving a focused, complete behavioral answer.

questions.q: What is the most common mistake candidates make with the STAR method?
options: Spending too much time on Situation and rushing through Result
Giving too much technical detail in Action
Not mentioning any numbers
Making the Task section too short
questions.explain: Interviewers remember the Action and Result most; spending most of the answer on backstory (Situation) and rushing the outcome weakens the answer.

questions.q: In the flash-sale incident STAR answer, what was the root cause traced to using golden signals and the USE method?
options: A bug in the checkout service's own code
A saturated database connection pool in the upstream inventory service
An expired PaymentPro API key
A Terraform state lock
questions.explain: The investigation traced the latency spike downstream to the external inventory service's saturated database connection pool, not to checkout's own code.

questions.q: Why does the near-miss secrets leak make a strong 'shift security left' story?
options: Because the key was successfully stolen and used
Because gitleaks caught the key before it was ever committed, avoiding a costly after-the-fact cleanup
Because it shows the team has no security tooling
Because it happened in production
questions.explain: Catching the leak at commit time, before it entered git history, meant no rotation or history-scrubbing was needed — demonstrating the value of catching issues early.

questions.q: What were the two concrete action items from the flash-sale incident's blameless postmortem?
options: Firing the engineer responsible and rewriting checkout from scratch
A new saturation alert and a circuit breaker in checkout
Switching cloud providers and deleting the inventory service
Removing all monitoring to reduce noise
questions.explain: The postmortem's action items were adding an earlier saturation alert (rather than only an exhaustion alert) and adding a circuit breaker so checkout degrades gracefully.
